en.title: Gather All Red Balls with Adjacent Swaps
en.description:
Each step swaps two adjacent balls. Make all R form one contiguous block, with W allowed on both sides. Find the minimum number of swaps; if it exceeds 10⁹, output −1. The source's example swap sequences changed the number of balls, so this site corrected them according to the explicit adjacent-swap rule.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: One line containing an R/W string. The source's range says 1..100000, but the statement explicitly requires a test with RW repeated 100000 times; this site keeps that case and supports lengths 1..200000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: swapping the final WR gives WRRRW in just 1 step; the source's answer of 2 has been corrected. Example 2: the red balls are at 2, 12, 14, and moving them to 11, 12, 13 takes 9+0+1=10 steps; the source's answer of 4 has been corrected. Example 3: there are no red balls, so 0 steps.
hints: The original positions p[i] of the red balls keep their relative order and move to the consecutive positions start+i; let b[i]=p[i]−i, minimize the sum of absolute distances to a common start, and take the median.
